summary: Up 0.1 on w12 (8.2). The trim A weave contrast is back and now matches py_37301 at studio distance: p8 back float cover 14.2 % (photo 14.6 %), high-pass 0.186 (0.188), p90/p50 1.31 (1.30). That was the w12 regression, now fixed. The gooseneck hose (about 0.4 of the head, py_37305 about 0.4) and the charcoal bezel are also fixed. The trim B petal backs on D/G read as py_37302's sliver print. Four things keep PY below 8.5. (1) The w12 sliver change also went onto the trim A EARS, because they share tex_py_confetti. py_37305's ear shows angular, notched sakura chips of mixed size plus many tiny specks (cover 17 %, chip/ground 2.5). Ours are uniform rice-grain slivers (cover 11 %, chip/ground 2.0) on a ground that is too blue (S 0.31 vs 0.20). (2) The pocket is better: the tray is in the lower part of the recess, the mesh follows the smile and there is no grey gap. But the recess still ends about 0.30 m (BH frame) above the shell's lower edge. In san_26, b_san_20 and san_14 the mesh bottom sits about 3-5 cm above the shell edge, with the footrest hanging right below it. (3) At close range (p5, q14, q13b foreground) the cloth is still a random axis-aligned mosaic of short bars. py_37301's cushion arranges its floats in vertical columns, and py_37306 in diagonal rows. (4) Small items: the navy flap is still dead flat, the cushion is desaturated (S 0.12 vs 0.18), and the placards are blank.
lighting_note: Not scored. q14 has a large white sun/specular blotch on the seat-back ahead (about x 490-560, y 310-420) that reads as a fabric defect; q13/q14 cabin exposure is bluer and more saturated than py_37302/37303 (D back S0.26 in q13 vs studio p3 0.23; py_37302 0.34 under its own blue cast). Studio colours were used for all colour judgements.

issues.fix: Split the tile. In make_swatches.py add synth_py_petal_ear (a copy of synth_py_confetti with e = uniform(1.1, 1.9), req = clip(normal(6.5, 2.5), 3, 11), 28 chips at min spacing 22 px, a notch depth of 0.35 on about 40 % of the chips, and about 140 tiny specks of 1-2.5 px at gain 1.5-2.5). issues.issue: The literature pocket and its recess still sit too high on the back shell. About 0.30 m (BH frame) of plain shell, plus a silver trim line, separates the recess bottom from the shell's lower edge. In real rear views the mesh bottom is about 3-5 cm above the shell edge, and the footrest brackets hang directly beneath it.
issues.evidence: san_26 (1136 px/m at the frame): recess from the placards (~y 600) to ~825, shell edge ~845, footrest ~855. b_san_20: about 3-4 cm grey lip between the mesh and the footrest pivots. san_14 (side-rear view): pocket contents end just above the shell's lower edge. Render p6: recess bottom y 205, silver line y 300-330, footrest y 400-440. Code: recess centre py0 + 0.12 = 0.47, h 0.25 (bottom 0.345); shell rear skin from ds[1] y 0.12; pyTrim at y 0.04.
issues.fix: Real photos win for geometry. Option A (no new triangles): in src/09b_py.js keep the screen and placards. Change the recess to gRBox(0.255, 0.20, ...) at on(0.52 ...) so its top stays 2 cm under the placards (bottom 0.42), and drop the lower plain shell by raising the rear-skin start ds[1] 0.12 -> 0.36 and the shell loft's first two sections to y 0.30 / 0.36, so the shell's rear lower edge sits about 4 cm under the recess. Move the footrest pivot and pyTrim (0.04 -> 0.33, or delete it; no silver line shows on the rear face in san_26 / b_san_20 / san_14) to just below. Check p7 so the lower shell doesn't open a gap at the cushion. Option B, if the shell height is load-bearing (py_37303 side profile): keep the shell, recess 0.255 x 0.40 (bottom about 0.20), tray scaled 1.2x in height and moved down to the bottom of the recess, and shell colour #6a7079 on a 0.04 lip only. Ask the user which (question 2).

issues.issue: At close range the trim A cloth is a random, axis-aligned mosaic of short bars (p5 cushion, q14 seat backs, q13b foreground). The official close-ups show organised float structure: in py_37301's cushion the short light floats stack into vertical columns, a ladder about 1 cm wide; py_37306 shows them in diagonal rows.
issues.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Calc/c6e420be-be6c-56c3-9e6e-efdc259c79f1/scratchpad/w13a_closefab.png: p5 | py_37306 corner | py_37301 cushion | q14. synth_py_back draws 8 columns jittered +-6 px with every other row shifted cw/4, and dim[] cells assigned randomly, so no column or diagonal survives.
issues.fix: make_swatches.py synth_py_back: remove the per-dash x jitter, rng.uniform(-6, 6) -> rng.uniform(-1.5, 1.5). Replace the alternating cw/4 shift with a slow twill drift x0 += (r * cw / 10) inside patches (drifting so a run reads diagonal for 4-6 rows). Make dim[] constant down a column for 3-6 rows (runs, not single cells) so light columns form. Keep the global stats (target studio float cover 13-15 %, high-pass 0.18-0.19) and recheck p8.
